body:
BLOCK exact candidate a00fc307a06591f711dd6e17f91156eb638028a5, narrowly on the missing direct-companion positive control. The owned `ProbeCartesianControl` is the right replacement for PlattScaling, and the unmodified exact focused suite passes 2/2 in an isolated clone. But the stated reason for dropping the second control is false: a same-run test companion can expose the exact direct syntax.

Independent clean mutation: I added `def fromProduct(_product: Product): ProbeCartesianControl = ProbeCartesianControl(0, "control")` to the test-only companion and added `assert(typeChecks("storymodel4s.probes.ProbeCartesianControl.fromProduct((1, \"a\"))"))`. After `alignJVM/clean`, the build compiled all 15 align main and 23 align test sources in one run; the focused suite passed 2/2. The same mutation also passed an incremental compile. Therefore `typeChecks` can reach an explicitly declared companion member from a same-run test source. What it cannot reach here is the compiler-synthesized empty-companion member, which is a different and narrower measurement.

This matters because the candidate duplicates the Mirror positive assertion but leaves the direct `CellCoordinates.fromProduct(???)` negative without its own same-syntax positive mechanism control. Mirror absence may currently entail absence of the compiler-generated door, but it does not entail absence of an explicitly declared direct door; the suite probes both for that reason.

Minimal repair: keep the test-owned Cartesian record, give its test-only companion an explicit direct `fromProduct(Product)` door, assert that exact direct expression type-checks, and retain the existing two CellCoordinates negatives. This adds no production vocabulary or invariant and satisfies both requested positive courts without a rot-prone production anchor. No shared checkout paths were edited.
